name: kx-results
description: Result service for ICF Kayak Cross competitions — desktop application with KX-Web publisher and ALGE Timy3 timing
_comment_dependencies: The server still has ZERO runtime dependencies: node:http + node:sqlite.
Electron and electron-builder are build-time only — `node server.js` runs
with nothing installed at all, exactly as before.
The one native dependency, serialport, belongs to timy-bridge and is now
installed with the application rather than by hand. Its binding is N-API,
so the prebuilt binary npm downloads loads unchanged in both Electron and
plain Node: no compiler, no toolchain, no electron-rebuild, and one
installation that serves both ways of running the software.
If the binding is missing anyway, nothing is broken: the bridge reports
serialport_available:false and Time Trial times are entered by hand.
_comment_build: asar is off. Packing the app into app.asar means the server is forked from a
path inside an archive and the archive is also the fork's cwd, which is where
the packaged build kept going wrong. Unpacked costs install size and lets
anyone read the source, neither of which matters for this software. Turn it
back on later if you want, but test a packaged build before a competition.
The launcher writes nothing next to the executable — kx.db, launcher.json,
timy-config.json and launcher.log all live in the per-user data folder, so an
installed copy under Program Files stays read-only.
electron-builder validates this block against a strict schema: any key it
does not know is a hard error, which is why these notes live out here.
nsis and portable both produce .exe, so each target names its own artifact;
a single top-level artifactName makes the second overwrite the first.
linux.desktop is omitted deliberately: in 26.x its generated schema types
the entry record as a function, so an object literal fails validation. The
.desktop file is derived from productName and description anyway.
